title: ActiveN: A Scalable and Flexibly-Programmable Event-Driven Neuromorphic Processor
problem: Most neuromorphic chips rely on custom circuits and on-chip memory for parameter storage, which limits programming flexibility and scalability as brain-inspired applications diversify. Storing all synapse data on-chip creates memory capacity bottlenecks.
motivation: Event-driven neuromorphic processors enable efficient brain-inspired computing, but current designs sacrifice either programming flexibility or memory scalability.
method: ActiveN builds a neuromorphic computer out of many standard RISC-V processors, each designed to handle messages that trigger computations instantly when neural spikes arrive. Instead of storing all synaptic connections (the weights between neurons) on the chip itself, the system keeps them in external memory like DRAM or HBM, which costs less and holds more data. A memory controller watches for sparse data (when connections are mostly zero or unused) and sends only the useful pieces directly to each processor, cutting down the delay. The instruction set includes efficient operations for both whole-number and decimal math, so different brain-inspired algorithms can all run on the same hardware without needing custom circuits.
key_novelty: ActiveN achieves scalable, flexible neuromorphic computing by replacing custom circuits with standard RISC-V processors that detect sparse patterns and store synaptic connections in external memory instead of on-chip storage.
contributions: RISC-V-based many-core neuromorphic architecture with active-message micro-architecture for event-driven SNN programming
Sparse data identification and direct forwarding mechanism in memory subsystem to mitigate latency penalties
Off-chip bulk storage support for synapse data enabling 512 processing units (10x more than prior work)
Customized instruction set with fixed-and floating-point operations providing flexible programmability across neural models

metrics.speedup: 7.9x vs neuromorphic chip with on-chip SRAM; 96.6x vs NVIDIA A100
metrics.other: 512 processing units (10x vs baseline); strong memory bandwidth utilization

baselines: State-of-the-art neuromorphic chip with custom circuitry and on-chip SRAM
primary_theme: Scalable event-driven neuromorphic processor with flexible programming
